final_answer:
Kocuria is NOT significantly associated with poor prognosis in this TCGA-LUAD cohort.

ANALYSIS SUMMARY:
- Cohort: 457 matched TCGA-LUAD patients with tumor microbiome and survival data (173 events, 284 censored).
- 82 of 250 microbiome genera had sufficient prevalence (>=10% nonzero) for testing.
- Univariate Cox Proportional Hazards analysis was performed on each genus.

POOR PROGNOSIS GENERA (HR > 1, p < 0.05, log1p-transformed):
Only 3 genera reached nominal significance: Anaerococcus (HR=1.457, p=0.021), Micrococcus (HR=1.187, p=0.025), and Staphylococcus (HR=1.116, p=0.044). None survived FDR correction (all q > 0.66).

KOCURIA RESULT:
- log1p model: HR = 1.064, 95% CI = [0.850, 1.332], p = 0.587 — NOT significant.
- Raw count model: HR = 1.011, 95% CI = [1.0004, 1.0226], p = 0.043 — borderline nominal significance, but the effect is negligible (1.1% hazard increase per read), the CI lower bound is barely above 1, and it does not survive FDR correction (q = 0.878).
- Kaplan-Meier log-rank (Kocuria+ vs Kocuria-): p = 0.593 — no significant survival difference.
- Kocuria was present in only 51/457 (11.2%) of samples.

CONCLUSION: Under the standard log1p transformation used for sparse microbiome count data, Kocuria shows no significant association with poor prognosis (p = 0.587, CI crosses 1). The borderline raw-count result is fragile and does not hold up to multiple-testing correction or the independent log-rank test. Kocuria is not a robust prognostic marker in this cohort.
